title: Differences between cloud and on-premises infrastructure

videos.script: This course is about defending what you run in somebody else's data centre. {{title}} You will not need a cloud account for any of it. {{lab}} Two programs on your own computer stand in for AWS. One is the real AWS command line. The other is moto, which answers it the way AWS would. {{moto}} This lesson builds that lab, and shows what to do when a step fails. Then it shows the difference the rest of the course rests on. {{rack}} On premises, changing the infrastructure means getting into a building. {{api}} In the cloud, it means holding a key. The controls are an API on the internet. {{one-call}} So a defence is a setting, and so is a failure. You will watch one request turn a private bucket public. {{curl}} A stranger asks for a file and is refused. One call later, the same stranger gets two patients' names. {{fix}} And one call turns it back. You will prove the fix the way the fault was found: by asking again, as the stranger. {{end}}
